lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use alternate star-shaped leaves, monoecious spherical flower heads and a woody multiple fruit of capsules to define the sweetgum branch.

project_scope.note: Altingiaceae is monogeneric under current Kew, containing Liquidambar.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the alternate palmately lobed star-shaped leaves, then look for separate male and female spherical inflorescences on the same tree. The female head matures into the familiar woody spiky sweetgum ball.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Deciduous resinous trees; leaves alternate, palmately 3–7-lobed with palmate venation; small deciduous stipules present.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Monoecious. Male flowers occur in clusters along terminal racemes; female flowers form pendent globose heads. Perianth is very reduced; ovary is semi-inferior/inferior, 2-locular with 2 persistent styles.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A spherical multiple fruit composed of many woody septicidal capsules with hardened persistent styles; seeds numerous and often winged.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Alternate star leaf + hanging spherical female head + woody spiky capsule-ball = Altingiaceae/Liquidambar.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: star leaf → male vs female heads → persistent paired styles → woody multiple fruit → Platanus comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Sweetgum is a whole-inflorescence fruit lesson: the spiky ball is not one fruit but a cluster of many capsules.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the alternate star-shaped leaf
steps.look_for: Palmately lobed leaf on an alternate node, not opposite.
steps.why_it_matters: This immediately helps separate sweetgum from maples.

steps.title: 2 · Split male and female flower heads
steps.look_for: Male stamen clusters in a terminal raceme; female flowers in separate pendent spherical heads.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows the monoecious reproductive architecture before fruit forms.

steps.title: 3 · Find the two persistent styles
steps.look_for: Each capsule unit bears paired style remnants that harden into the spikes of the mature ball.
steps.why_it_matters: Explains where the 'spikes' of a sweetgum ball come from.

steps.title: 4 · Break down the sweetgum ball
steps.look_for: Many individual woody capsules packed into one spherical head, each releasing small seeds.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents calling the entire ball a single capsule.

comparisons.title: Altingiaceae vs Platanaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have large palmately lobed leaves and ball-like fruits. Sweetgum leaves are alternate and its ball is a woody cluster of capsules with hard style spikes; Platanus has mottled bark and fuzzy achene heads.

comparisons.title: Altingiaceae vs Acer
comparisons.rule: Sweetgum leaves are alternate; maples are opposite. Fruit also differs: sweetgum capsule balls versus paired samaras.

visual_lesson.caveat: Leaf shape alone is not enough—maples and sycamores can look similar. Use leaf arrangement plus fruit architecture.

genera.fast_cue: alternate star-shaped leaves + spherical female heads + woody spiky multiple fruit

visual_targets.annotation_goal: show how each capsule contributes two spikes
